title: Obsolescence Replacement of the Business Cabin Seat Display Units
abstract: The display panel used in the business cabin seat monitors goes out of production in 2027. This proposal captures a like-for-like replacement with a current panel and the seat-side changes it forces.

sections.reason: The panel supplier issued an end-of-production notice in April 2026 with a last-time-buy in the third quarter of 2027. Spares consumption across the delivered fleet runs at about 340 units a year, so a last-time-buy would need a seven-figure commitment and eight years of storage for a component with a shelf life problem. Two operators have already asked what the forward path is. There is no in-service defect: the current unit performs to specification and its reliability is within the contracted figure.
sections.description: The proposal is a replacement display unit built on a current panel with the same active area, the same bezel envelope and the same mounting pattern, so that the seat shroud is untouched. The head end lining D4420127058194 needs a local cut-out change because the new unit is 4 mm deeper at the connector end, and the stowage rail D4420126873973 is re-drilled to clear it. Protective sleeving AES430915-41 is added on the seat-side harness where it now passes closer to the seat frame. Arrangement is on drawing D44201139715. Work is at the seat, zones 221 and 241. The cabin panel 9RK, the lower lining 56RK3 and the upper latch 695RK are all disturbed during removal and refitted unchanged.
sections.effects: Estimated mass reduction of 0.35 kg per seat, which is about 14 kg on a typical business cabin. Electrical load reduced by 9 VA per unit. Interchangeable at the seat, so an operator may change units as the old ones fail rather than in one campaign, which is the strong argument for this option. No change to the head end server, to the content path or to the cabin crew interface. The illustrated parts content needs a pre and post item pair, and the seat display removal task needs a note on the deeper connector clearance.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit and spares only. Nothing prevents an operator embodying seat by seat during normal maintenance. A production cut-in would be needed before the last-time-buy date if the delivered standard is not to become unsupportable.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the deeper connector envelope clears every seat variant in the delivered fleet, and whether the head end server software standard needs to change to drive the new panel timing.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in required before the panel last-time-buy date in the third quarter of 2027
